# dsh-session-hub
English | 中文
## Summary
A third-party DeepSeek Harness plugin that lists every Session across every Workspace on one page, o
rdered by day by default, with search over title and Workspace path, running and archived filters, a
nd a per-Workspace colour that survives sorting. The shipped sidebar browses Workspaces first; this
page offers the other path — locate by when, recognise by where — for installations where Workspaces
and Sessions have both grown past what a grouped list can show at a glance. It registers the keyed
`main` panel `session-hub` and the `sidebar.panellist` entry of the same id, reads the existing `ses
sions.list` and `workspaces.list` snapshots, and replaces no shipped surface.
## Use this package
Install it into a profile and enable the bundle; the sidebar gains one icon beside the Automation ta
sks entry, and that icon opens the page in the main column without selecting or activating a Session
ks entry, and that icon opens the page in the main column without selecting or activating a Session.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The page requires no configuration and registers no settings row. Its header states the Session coun
t and the number of Workspaces those Sessions belong to, and the four-way order control beside it is
the page's only mode switch: **By day** (the default), **Recent activity**, **By workspace**, and *
only mode switch: **By day** (the default), **Recent activity**, **By workspace**, and **By title**.
### The day view
**By day** groups the list under sticky local-date headings — `Today`, `Yesterday`, then a month-and
-day label that gains its year once the date leaves the current year — and each row's leading cell i
s the local clock time of its last prompt. Rows inside a day are newest first. This is the view the
plugin exists for: a Session is usually recalled as "the one from Tuesday afternoon in that project"
, and the day heading plus the clock column answer that without reading a single title.
**By workspace** groups under the Workspace's stored title with its full path as the group detail, i
n Workspace group order, and appends Sessions outside every Workspace under `No workspace`. **Recent
activity** and **By title** are flat lists; **By title** sorts on the session title and falls back
to recency for equal titles, so untitled Sessions collect at the end instead of scattering.
### Search and filters
The search field is a case-insensitive substring match over three values at once: the Session title,
its Workspace's title, and its Workspace's stored path. Typing a directory name therefore narrows t
he page to that Workspace without a separate Workspace filter, and typing part of a Session id does
not match, because ids never enter the page. Escape clears a non-empty query without closing the pag
t match, because ids never enter the page. Escape clears a non-empty query without closing the page.
Two chips filter the list: **Running** keeps only Sessions with running work, and **Include archived
** adds archived Sessions, which otherwise stay hidden. Archived rows keep their position in the cho
sen order, render dimmed, and carry an `Archived` tag; pinned Sessions carry a `Pinned` tag and stay
pinned in every order rather than leading it.
The order, both filters, and nothing else persist in browser-local storage under `dsh.session-hub.vi
ew`, so a reload restores the page as it was left. The query is deliberately not persisted: a stale
filter that hides every row is worse than retyping it.
### Rows and identification
Every row is one button that opens its Session through `uiWorkspace.openSession`, and every row carr
ies four identification values: the per-Workspace colour bar and dot, the Session title, the Workspa
ce title, and the turn count. The colour is derived from the Workspace id by a stable hash, so one W
orkspace keeps one hue across reloads, across orders, and across every Session in it; the same hue t
ints the small dot inside the meta line, which is what makes two Sessions from different Workspaces
distinguishable before their titles are read. The turn count comes from the Session's `sessionStats`
projection and is omitted when that projection is absent or reports zero turns, so a fresh scratch
Session does not read as a serious one.
A Session without a title renders the localized `Untitled` label in italic grey rather than an empty
title line, and hovering a row shows its absolute timestamp together with the Workspace path. Sessi
ons with `origin: 'subagent'` and unopened blank Sessions never appear: they are addressable through
their parent, not as history rows.
### Paging
The page renders at most 200 rows at a time and a `Show more` action appends the next batch; the foo
ter states how many rows remain. The limit resets whenever the order, a filter, or the query changes
, so a new view never inherits the previous scroll depth.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
- **No content in the list.** Rows show metadata only. Titles generated from the first prompt are tr
uncated by the Host around 20 characters, so Sessions whose titles collide — the same prompt run rep
eatedly, for example — remain distinguishable only by Workspace, day, time, and turn count. A prompt

excerpt would need a per-Session history read, which this plugin deliberately does not issue.
- **N
o Session lifecycle actions.** The page opens, orders, filters, and searches; it does not delete, ar

chive, rename, export, or fork. Those verbs stay with the sidebar and the packages that own them.
-
**No virtualization.** Rendering is batched at 200 rows rather than windowed, which keeps a few thou

sand Sessions responsive but is not designed for tens of thousands.
- **Archived and blank Sessions

are hidden by default** and blank ones cannot be reached from this page at all.
- **The live status
is running, not pending interaction.** When the surface supplies its status hook the row's dot follo
ws the real running state; it never reports an approval or a question waiting for an answer.
